description: I'm an aspiring aerospace engineer fascinated by space exploration, astrophysics, wormholes, and the mysteries of the universe. I love researching space-related concepts and learning how science and engineering could shape the future of space travel.
summary:
MARSBOUND: PROJECT NEW DAWN is an interactive Mars exploration game designed as a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. Players become astronauts stranded on Mars and must explore their surroundings, scan geological features, collect resources, repair equipment and establish a small outpost with help from A.R.I.A., an SI companion.

The game incorporates real NASA information through its interactive Discovery Archive, where players unlock scientific discoveries, learn about Mars geography and explore information from NASA missions. Players also experience simplified astronaut mission concepts such as oxygen management, resource planning and habitat construction.

By transforming space science into an interactive experience, our project encourages curiosity, critical thinking and interest in STEM among younger audiences. It addresses the challenge by making astronaut exploration and scientific learning more accessible, engaging and hands-on. Our goal is to inspire the next generation to explore, discover and imagine humanity's future beyond Earth.
details:
MARSBOUND: PROJECT NEW DAWN

A Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

MARSBOUND: PROJECT NEW DAWN is an interactive Mars exploration game designed to introduce young people to the challenges, science and problem-solving involved in human space exploration.

In the game, players take on the role of an astronaut whose spacecraft crash-lands on Mars. With assistance from A.R.I.A. (Autonomous Research, Intelligence and Assistance), an onboard super-intelligence companion, players must explore the Martian environment, scan geological features, collect resources, craft repair components, restore damaged systems and establish a small outpost.

Players can choose between three real Martian locations: Jezero Crater, Elysium Planitia and Valles Marineris. Each location introduces different geographical features and scientific context. Through exploration and scanning, players unlock entries in the NASA Discovery Archive, which provides descriptions of real Mars science, relevant NASA missions and links to official NASA sources.

The game also introduces simplified astronaut mission concepts, including oxygen management, stamina, equipment repair, habitat construction and scientific investigation. An optional greenhouse module introduces the importance of controlled-environment plant research for future space exploration.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our project aims to make space science more engaging, interactive and accessible to younger audiences. Instead of simply reading about Mars, players actively explore, investigate and make decisions within a simulated mission.

The experience encourages curiosity about planetary science, critical thinking, resource management and problem-solving. By connecting gameplay with NASA discoveries and research, we hope to inspire young people to learn more about STEM subjects and consider future opportunities in science, technology and space exploration.

Technology and Development Tools

The project was developed using JavaScript, HTML and CSS, with the browser's Canvas 2D API used to create its custom 2.5D game environment. The visual experience uses perspective, scrolling Martian landscapes, character sprites and environmental effects to create an immersive exploration experience without requiring a full 3D game engine. All sound effects and ambient audio are generated live with the Web Audio API, and the optional voice for A.R.I.A., the in-game AI assistant, uses the browser's built-in speech synthesis, so the game needs no audio files and no external services.

The game is built to be lightweight and accessible on the devices students actually use. It uses no game engine, no third-party code libraries and no installation. The entire game is under 1 MB, about 190 KB when compressed, compared with the tens or hundreds of megabytes typical of browser games built in engines such as Unity. It therefore loads quickly even on slow or crowded school Wi-Fi, and once loaded it keeps working if the connection drops. The game monitors its own frame rate and automatically lowers its rendering resolution on slower hardware, so it stays smooth on low-cost school Chromebooks and older laptops. It also pauses its animation when the tab is hidden, to save battery and processing power.

The game is designed to be safe for young players. It has no user accounts, no logins, no advertising, no chat and no in-game purchases, and it collects no personal information. Progress is saved only in the player's own browser and is never sent to a server. The only text a player enters, their astronaut's name, is filtered and checked before it is displayed. The game is hosted on Vercel and served over secure HTTPS, and links to NASA's websites open safely in a new tab. For accessibility, all spoken lines are also shown as subtitles, and a reduced-motion setting limits on-screen animation for players who need it.

We used Visual Studio Code as our development environment, Claude Code as an AI-assisted coding tool, and Git and GitHub for version control and project collaboration. The game runs in any modern web browser on Windows, macOS and ChromeOS.

NASA's official websites and mission resources, including NASA Mars Exploration, Mars Trek, the Perseverance mission and the Curiosity mission, were used to support the scientific information presented in the game. Every fact in the in-game NASA Discovery Archive was checked against the NASA page it cites and is labelled as either confirmed or interpretation. Each entry links directly to its NASA or JPL source, and fictional game events are clearly marked as fiction so they are never mistaken for real NASA discoveries.

Creativity and Innovation

A key creative feature is A.R.I.A., the astronaut's SI companion, which provides contextual guidance, explains scientific discoveries and helps players understand mission objectives.

Another central feature is the NASA Discovery Archive. It transforms scientific information into an interactive collection that grows as players explore and scan the Martian environment. This connects the player's actions directly to scientific learning.

The combination of astronaut role-playing, interactive exploration, resource management, scientific discovery and outpost construction turns Mars exploration into a short, story-driven learning experience.

Design Considerations

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, gameplay length, usability and technical limitations. We aimed to create an experience that could be completed in approximately 15–20 minutes while still providing meaningful exploration and learning.

We distinguished real NASA scientific information from fictional gameplay elements, avoided presenting simplified game mechanics as real engineering systems, and included official sources so players could explore the science further.

Our ultimate goal is to help the next generation imagine what it means to explore another planet.
